correctness.rationale: Set C=n/y and exchange a counted divisor d for t=n/d. The interval becomes C/λ ≤ t < C, preserving exactly the two endpoint conventions. For at least r candidates, the smallest u and r-th v give u+r−1 ≤ v < C ≤ λu, hence u≥a and C>b. For b<C≤min(b+1,λa), λ(a−1)≤b−1<C and t<C≤b+1 force the integer candidates to be exactly a through b. Thus precisely r divisors qualify if L divides n and fewer otherwise. Counting multiples in (by,X] gives the clipped floor difference, valid at X=by and Ty. Since λa>b and b+1>b, the first multiple strictly above by is included if y≥L/(T−b); its overshoot is in (0,L], giving the sharp slope. For λ=2 this yields a=r, b=2r−1, T=2r and the three listed LCMs. The exact rational checker and verification notes were inspected, not run; their finite range is not used for the proof. The frozen proof supplies replayable steps in RESULT.md lines 36–45.
